changed_reading.after: The ayah diagnoses idolatry as a deliberately built social bond: the shared object stabilizes belonging for a time, then the bond's own members disown and expel one another.
changed_reading.before: The ayah condemns a group for worshipping idols and predicts that its members will quarrel in the hereafter.

seeds.focus_anchor: The construction اتخذتم ... أوثانا مودة بينكم joins deliberate idol-taking to affection located in the space between the group.

changed_reading.after: The ending completes a protection-system reversal: what was taken as a sheltering alliance yields an anti-shelter, and the mutual support embodied in the alliance proves nonexistent.
changed_reading.before: The verse adds fire and lack of help as two punishments after the social quarrel.

seeds.focus_anchor: The close مأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين answers the earlier taking of substitutes apart from God with an imposed refuge and the absence of helpers.

changed_reading.after: The idol-mediated affection is structurally time-bounded: it is fitted to the near world's interests, and the act of standing for judgment removes the conditions that made it work.
changed_reading.before: Worldly friendship happens to end when judgment begins.

seeds.focus_anchor: The explicit span في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة places affection on one side of a temporal threshold and reciprocal rejection on the other.

changed_reading.after: The affection is also a governance mechanism: intimate bonds make demands for cultic conformity effective even when the affection itself remains genuine.
changed_reading.before: The group's affection is merely a pleasant by-product of common worship.

changed_reading.after: The affection can be authentic inside a bounded role-system while lacking value beyond it; resurrection ends the game that assigned the idols and alliances their social payoff.

changed_reading.after: Between you is also a field of accountability: the bond operates before a witness, and its final mutual accusations expose what group consensus had concealed.

changed_reading.after: As an exploratory lexical echo, affection itself approaches idol-form: the group not only loves through an idol but can objectify and venerate the bond that joins it.

seeds.focus_anchor: The adjacent focus words أوثانا مودة place an idol class beside a W-D-D noun whose branch inventory also contains a named idol.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the cultic image helps constitute an inside by policing an outside; at judgment that expelling function rotates inward and every former insider treats another as the one to be driven out.
changed_reading.before: Mutual cursing is only verbal hostility after the bond has vanished.

seeds.focus_anchor: The focus moves from worshipped images and affection between insiders to each part expelling the other through curse.

changed_reading.after: With careful containment, the fire can also be heard as the material completion of a نائرة already ignited between former allies: their refuge is the hostility their bond concealed.
changed_reading.before: The social collapse and the fire are consecutive but functionally separate outcomes.

seeds.focus_anchor: The focus places mutual repudiation and cursing immediately before مأواكم النار, all within the same collapsing group.
